name: Reflex displacement inside a TrendFlex regime
note: Ehlers' SuperSmoother feeds two orthogonal statistics built from the same filtered series: Reflex, the mean gap between the filtered price and the straight line joining it to its value n bars ago, and TrendFlex, the same difference-sum without the slope added back. Both are divided by the square root of an EWMA of their own square, so they read as self-calibrating standard errors and one threshold means the same thing on every symbol. TrendFlex gives the regime; a fresh Reflex cross down through -disp inside an up regime is a measured displacement below the zero-lag trend line, and that is the long entry. Exit when Reflex is reclaimed past +rf_exit, when TrendFlex loses its sign, or on the time stop. Threshold sanity, measured rather than assumed: on real 5-minute bars |Reflex| has a median near 0.62 and a 99th percentile near 2.5, so the published 2.5 setting produces 0-6 gated crosses in 6,000 bars and is not a signal at all. The swept displacements are therefore 1.0/1.5/2.0, which sit at roughly the 75th, 90th and 97th percentiles of the statistic.
source: John F. Ehlers, 'Reflex: A New Zero-Lag Indicator', Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, February 2020. Slope-detrended difference sum, the 0.04/0.96 mean-square EWMA and the division by sqrt(MS) verified against github.com/MathisWellmann/go_ehlers_indicators, file re_flex.go. The TrendFlex-gated displacement entry is the harvested synthesis.
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    import math
    bars = ctx.bars
    N = len(bars)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    n = int(ctx.p.n)
    k = float(ctx.p.ss)
    al = float(ctx.p.alpha)
    # --- SuperSmoother (2-pole Butterworth), Ehlers' constants ---
    a1 = math.exp(-1.414213562373095 * math.pi / k)
    b1 = 2.0 * a1 * math.cos(1.414213562373095 * math.pi / k)
    c2 = b1
    c3 = -a1 * a1
    c1 = 1.0 - c2 - c3
    f = [0.0] * N
    for j in range(N):
        p0 = c[j]
        p1 = c[j - 1] if j >= 1 else p0
        f1 = f[j - 1] if j >= 1 else p0
        f2 = f[j - 2] if j >= 2 else p0
        f[j] = c1 * (p0 + p1) * 0.5 + c2 * f1 + c3 * f2
    # --- Reflex and TrendFlex from the same filtered series ---
    rf = [None] * N
    tf = [None] * N
    msr = 0.0
    mst = 0.0
    sq = math.sqrt
    inv_n = 1.0 / n
    for j in range(n + 2, N):
        fj = f[j]
        slope = (f[j - n] - fj) * inv_n
        sr = 0.0
        st = 0.0
        for q in range(1, n + 1):
            d = fj - f[j - q]
            st += d
            sr += d + q * slope
        sr *= inv_n
        st *= inv_n
        msr = al * sr * sr + (1.0 - al) * msr
        mst = al * st * st + (1.0 - al) * mst
        if msr > 0.0:
            rf[j] = sr / sq(msr)
        if mst > 0.0:
            tf[j] = st / sq(mst)
    ctx.rf = ctx.series(rf, "reflex")
    ctx.tf = ctx.series(tf, "trendflex")


def signal(ctx, i):
    if i < 1:
        return 0
    r = ctx.rf[i]
    pr = ctx.rf[i - 1]
    t = ctx.tf[i]
    if r is None or pr is None or t is None:
        return 0
    d = float(ctx.p.disp)
    # a FRESH displacement below the zero-lag line while the regime is up
    if t > 0.0 and r <= -d and pr > -d:
        return 1
    if t < 0.0 and r >= d and pr < d:
        return -1
    return 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    r = ctx.rf[i]
    t = ctx.tf[i]
    if r is None or t is None:
        return False
    x = float(ctx.p.rf_exit)
    if ctx.positions[0]["side"] == "long":
        return r >= x or t < 0.0
    return r <= -x or t > 0.0
